verdict.line: You lose if you sit in Tongue Lash range and let his stacks and Thick Skin regen outheal your pokes before level 6; you win if you delay the all-in until Hydra/Trinity Force are online and strike the instant his Q is down.

brief.thesis: Tahm Kench's Q (Tongue Lash) threatens from 900 range on a 7-to-5-second cooldown, slows on hit, and stacks An Acquired Taste toward a stun (or a Devour from level 6 on), while his passive's health-scaled damage and Thick Skin's out-of-combat regen let him win any fight that drags past the first exchange. Fiora has no ranged answer and only a 750-range Riposte parry to punish him, so the 47.1% win rate over 191 games reflects a lane decided by patience, not aggression, through level 6.

tell.watch: Tahm's An Acquired Taste stack count

theirWindow.what: He's hunting the third stack with Q or an auto. Before level 6 that stack stuns you and resets his damage window; from level 6 on it lets him Devour you outright. Back off auto range the moment you're at 2.

yourWindow.when: his Q (Tongue Lash) just went on cooldown
yourWindow.what: With his only slow/stun tool down, double-dash Lunge (Q can be used twice within a couple seconds) into a held Riposte parry and commit before Thick Skin's regen and his health-scaled passive heal the trade back.

start.why: Taken in 90.3% of games and the lifesteal proc stacks with Duelist, giving you the sustain to survive early Q pokes without a potion refresh you can't afford to take.

boots.why: Picked in 62.9% of games for a 54.5% win rate; every one of Tahm's damage sources (Q, W, R) is magic, so the tenacity and MR directly blunt his poke and his Devour burst.

core.why: The highest-winrate path (75% over 28 games) starts here; it gives sustained damage and wave pressure while you're still too weak to force skirmishes.
Adds the burst and move speed that make a double-Lunge all-in actually land before Thick Skin's regen kicks in.
Lets you tank through his passive's health-scaled damage during the all-in and heal the delayed damage back after.

situational.when: you're ahead and want a burst reset to punish him before he can Thick Skin shield
the lane stays passive and you need extra sustain to out-scale his health stacking
his team's magic damage (including his own Q/W/R) is piling up and you need the shield

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards the sustained hits your double-Lunge-into-auto trade pattern already produces, marking Tahm for bonus damage right as your all-in lands.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport posts the highest win rate in this matchup (50% vs Flash+Ignite's 47.3%); since the lane is defensive until items come online, Teleport lets you reset a losing wave or join a side objective instead of forcing a fight you can't yet win.

playing.title: Respect Q range pre-6
playing.detail: Tongue Lash reaches 900 range and slows on hit while stacking An Acquired Taste. Don't walk into free pokes, especially before level 3 when you have the least HP to spare.

playing.title: Track your own stack count
playing.detail: At 3 stacks you either get stunned by his next Q (pre-6) or become Devour-able (6+). Disengage the instant you're at 2.

playing.title: Trade only after his Q whiffs
playing.detail: The moment Tongue Lash is down (5-7s depending on rank), double-dash with Lunge and hold Riposte for the parry before he can reapply the slow.

playing.title: Save Riposte for his real auto
playing.detail: Riposte parries his next basic attack and reflects magic damage. Hold it to shut down a hit once his health-scaled passive damage is actually threatening, not on cooldown.

playing.title: Delay all-ins until Hydra/Trinity
playing.detail: You have no decisive extended-trade tool off just Doran's Blade. Play the wave, not the duel, until your core items land around level 9-11.

playing.title: Punish before level 6 Devour
playing.detail: Before he hits 6 there's no removal threat from Devour, only the Q stun. This is your safest window to force a short fight.

playing.title: Use Blade Waltz to end fights, not start them
playing.detail: Successive Blade Waltz strikes on the same target deal less damage, so commit it to close a fight quickly rather than chip poke, since his Thick Skin shield and passive reward drawn-out trades.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and all win-rate figures are measured from current-patch OP.GG games; the mechanical reasoning and timing calls are this brief's own analysis, not sourced from that data.
